\subsection{Testing/Debugging Tools}


\subsubsection{rst2pseudoxml%
  \label{rst2pseudoxml-py}%
}

\begin{DUfieldlist}
\item[{Reader:}]
Standalone

\item[{Parser:}]
reStructuredText

\item[{Writer:}]
%
\phantomsection\label{pseudo-xml}Pseudo-XML
\end{DUfieldlist}

\texttt{rst2pseudoxml} is used for debugging the Docutils \textquotedbl{}Reader to
Transform to Writer\textquotedbl{} pipeline.  It produces a compact pretty-printed
\textquotedbl{}pseudo-XML\textquotedbl{}, where nesting is indicated by indentation (no end-tags).
External attributes for all elements are output, and internal
attributes for any leftover \textquotedbl{}pending\textquotedbl{} elements are also given.


\section{Customization}

All front-end tools support the options/settings from the generic
\href{config.html\#configuration-file-sections-entries}{configuration file sections} plus the sections of their components
(reader, writer, parser).
Some front-end tools also add application-specific settings.


\subsection{Command-Line Options%
  \label{command-line-options}%
}

Command-line options are intended for one-off customization.
They take priority over configuration file settings.

Use the \texttt{-{}-help} option on each of the front ends to list the
command-line options it supports.


\subsection{Configuration Files%
  \label{configuration-files}%
}

Configuration files are used for persistent customization; they can be
set once and take effect every time you use a front-end tool.

Command-line options and their corresponding configuration file entry
names are listed in the \href{config.html}{Docutils Configuration} document.
